subject: Renewal: Xcelera — flexible commit + price-lock proposal
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Asha Iyer <asha.iyer@xcelera.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — flexible commit + price-lock proposal

Hi Asha,

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Xcelera's usage growth has been great to see — congrats on the new vector search rollout. With your renewal coming up next month, I wanted to put a short note outlining a proposal that should make the transition smoother for you and protect against price volatility on our side.

High level proposal (attached: Xcelera_MAProposal_v3.pdf, commit_breakdown.xlsx):
- 12-month term with a flexible commit ladder instead of a single front-loaded commit (monthly commit floors + 2x burst capacity).
- Price-lock for the first 6 months at current unit rates, then a small scheduled CPI-linked adjustment thereafter (we can cap annual increases at 5%).
- One-time operational credit equal to 6% of the annual committed spend to offset migration/validation work.

I realize procurement will want something tighter on guarantees and our legal team will want to align contract language. If you can share a rough preferred commit cadence (monthly/quarterly) and who from procurement should be looped in, I can route an internal approval path and get a redline-ready term sheet over.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call on Wednesday to walk through the numbers?

Best,
Sean
Account Exec — Enterprise Renewals
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: Xcelera_MAProposal_v3.pdf (proposal), commit_breakdown.xlsx (usage model)

From: Asha Iyer <asha.iyer@xcelera.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Whitmore <t.whitmore@xcelera.ai>, Procurement <procurement@xcelera.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — flexible commit + price-lock proposal

Hi Sean,

Appreciate the summary and the attachments — that looks sensible. A few quick notes from our side:
- We prefer monthly commit floors (easier for our finance team) but would like the ability to shift up to +/-20% of committed spend quarter-to-quarter to reflect product seasonality.
- The 6% operational credit is a good start; procurement will push for a multi-year credit schedule or an upfront service credit.
- Legal will want the price-lock wording tightened; can you confirm whether the cap is firm or a guideline?

I'm available Wednesday 3/17 at 10am PT for a call. I've looped Tom (VP of Product) and our procurement mailbox.

Thanks,
Asha
Head of Platform — Xcelera
asha.iyer@xcelera.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Asha Iyer <asha.iyer@xcelera.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 12:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — flexible commit + price-lock proposal

Thanks Asha — that's helpful.

Two quick clarifications for the call and to set expectations internally:
- Monthly commit floors with +/-20% seasonal shift: we can accommodate this with a sliding reconciliation model; I'll attach a sample runway (commit_breakdown.xlsx) showing how the ladder would look.
- Price-lock: our commercial team prefers to commit to a firm 6-month lock at current rates with a clearly defined schedule after. We can cap annual increases at 5% and include a mutual termination right if material changes in compute pricing occur.

Camila / Grace — can you confirm whether a 6% one-time credit is approvable at SE (sales engineering) level or if this needs revenue ops sign-off? If the customer pushes for a multi-year diluted credit, we should know thresholds.

Sean

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — flexible commit + price-lock proposal

Sean — quick internal note after reviewing the numbers:
- A 6% one-time credit is within SDR-level promotional authority but anything that effectively reduces list price over multiple years needs RevOps approval.
- If the customer wants a multi-year amortized credit (e.g., 2%/year over 3 years) we should treat that as a pricing concession tied to a higher commit band. Recommend the following conditional offer to present on the call:
  * Base: 12-month term, monthly commit floors, 6-month firm price-lock, 6% one-time operational credit.
  * Upsell incentive: If Xcelera commits to a 20% higher annual spend band, convert the one-time credit into an additional 2% annual discount over the subsequent 2 years (capped).
- Also confirm whether we can include a one-time migration SLA credit (service days) for any production incidents in the first 90 days post-migration — that can be an easy bargaining chip.

Marissa — please pull any historical usage variance for Xcelera for the last 6 quarters so we can model the +/-20% movement.

Camila
Director, Commercial Ops

From: Asha Iyer <asha.iyer@xcelera.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Whitmore <t.whitmore@xcelera.ai>, Procurement <procurement@xcelera.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — flexible commit + price-lock proposal

Thanks — that conditional structure looks workable. A few items from the call notes:
- We like the migration SLA credit idea; can you quantify (service days or $) and include it in the term sheet?
- We'd prefer any multi-year discount to be automatic once commit thresholds are met rather than retroactive; that avoids reconciliation headaches.
- On price-lock cap: we need the language to state the 5% annual cap is firm and outline what would trigger mutual termination.

We ran a quick internal model and would be open to the 20% higher commit band if you can make the annual discount conversion 2.5% (instead of 2%) and include a one-time 3% prepayment credit if we prepay 50% of committed spend for year one. Pricing/levers below for negotiation: 
- Base: 6% operational credit, 6-month price-lock, monthly floors, +/-20% seasonal shift.
- Xcelera ask: convert credit to 2.5% annual discount on >20% commit uplift; 3% prepay credit for 50% prepayment; migration SLA credit (5 service days or $35k).

Let's draft final term sheet after you confirm the prepay credit and conversion rates.

Asha

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Asha Iyer <asha.iyer@xcelera.ai>, Tom Whitmore <t.whitmore@xcelera.ai>, Procurement <procurement@xcelera.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Final terms for signature — Xcelera renewal (draft)

Hi all — thanks for the productive conversation this week. Internal has greenlit the following draft commercial terms for the renewal; attached is an updated term sheet and a draft DocuSign envelope: Xcelera_MAProposal_v3.pdf.

Final commercial summary (draft for legal/PO):
- Term: 12 months starting on contract execution.
- Commit: monthly commit floors (customer reports monthly), +/-20% permitted movement quarter-to-quarter with reconciliation.
- Price lock: firm 6 months at current unit rates; thereafter CPI-linked adjustment capped at 5% annually. Mutual termination clause if major cloud compute index moves >30%.
- Credits: 6% one-time operational credit applied on execution. If customer elects to prepay >=50% of Y1 commit, an additional 3% prepayment credit applies.
- Upsell conversion: If annual committed spend increases by >=20% vs prior year, the 6% one-time credit converts to a 2.5% annual discount for the following 2 years (applies prospectively, not retroactive).
- Migration SLA: up to 5 service days credit or $35,000 credit for qualifying production-impact incidents within the first 90 days.

Next steps:
1) Asha / Tom: confirm PO process and whether you can route the 50% prepay option.
2) Procurement: if this is acceptable, we'll send a redline-ready contract and DocuSign link.
3) Marissa / Camila: I'll include your modeling and finalize the commit ladder in the contract exhibits.

If there are no material changes by end of day Monday we'll issue the DocuSign envelope for signature.

Thanks,
Sean
Account Exec — Enterprise Renewals
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: Xcelera_MAProposal_v3.pdf (updated term sheet), commit_breakdown.xlsx (final commit ladder)
